clue.text: 8 20 of 7 delivering gigantic address

indicators.note: delivering a speech means turning words out in a new form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A former Elysée resident gives a vast speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is built from cross-references: 8 (CI-DEVANT, former), 20 (HABITANT, inhabitant) of 7 (the Elysée Palace), so a former French president.
explanation.definitionFit: Valéry was President of France 1974-81, so a one-time resident of the presidential palace.

clue.text: 8 20 of 7 from the centre of Paris

definitions.meaning: former inhabitant of the presidential palace in Paris, a past French president
the Pompidou Centre, the arts complex in Paris named after this president

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: 'the centre' is not the middle of Paris but the Centre named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: He was French president 1969-74, and the Beaubourg arts centre bears his name.

clue.text: Vichy leader with story about Louis XIV's mistress

parts.note: Pierre Laval headed the government of Vichy France
a story is a lie, a fib
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A wartime collaborator tells tales about the Sun King's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Louise de La Vallière was a mistress of Louis XIV in the 1660s.

clue.text: Castle where Walpole ran into Bismark?

indicators.note: ran goes into the middle of the statesman's first name

parts.note: Otto von Bismarck, the German chancellor, so his first name

explanation.surface: Asks where the novelist Walpole bumped into the Iron Chancellor.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace Walpole wrote the Gothic novel The Castle of Otranto; the question mark flags Bismarck standing for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Otranto is the castle in the title of Horace Walpole's 1764 Gothic novel.

clue.text: See 12
8 20 of 7 turned out to be a legal scheduler

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are tipped out and rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A former president is revealed as a mere legal timetabler.
explanation.definitionFit: The general led Free France and became first president of the Fifth Republic, a past palace resident.

clue.text: Where 1, 2 and 6 all appeared in "The Bill", see? Look mate, 'e's finished!

indicators.note: finished says this last piece comes at the very end of the build

parts.note: taken as written
Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in England
look means see
a mate is a pal
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
the Cockney 'e is simply the letter E

explanation.surface: A Cockney police-drama fan points out three presidents appearing on The Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bill' is a long-running British TV police drama, but here 'The' and 'Bill' are separate pieces; 'finished' puts E last.
explanation.definitionFit: The palace in Paris is the official residence of French presidents, where all three lived.

clue.text: As 1, 2 and 6 are unable to bear one of the French 5

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the word for unable carries the other pieces inside it

parts.note: unable means can't
one is I as a Roman numeral
de is French for of
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Three presidents cannot cope with a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means former, as all three are former presidents.

clue.text: Ornithograph that's showing presence of thrush

indicators.note: the run of letters is present inside these clue words, showing through them

explanation.surface: A bird-recording instrument detects a thrush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrush' looks like the bird, prompted by 'Ornithograph', but it is the mouth infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphtha is a medical term for the fungal mouth infection called thrush.

clue.text: Old slag fell out of old scripture

annotationWithheld.why: Old slag fell out of old scripture (6), SCORIA: slag is the definition, but no parse of 'fell out of old scripture' gives the letters, and no blog or database was found to explain it
annotationWithheld.clue: Old slag fell out of old scripture

clue.text: Sleepy royal butter provider might, perhaps, deny Lear

indicators.note: perhaps flags a possible rearrangement of what follows, the letters as they might be

explanation.surface: A drowsy cow could refuse King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: In A. A. Milne's poem The King's Breakfast, the Alderney cow who supplies butter for the king answers 'sleepily'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cow breed from this Channel Island provides butter for the king's bread in Milne's poem.

clue.text: Artistic licence?

parts.note: artistic licence read as unrestricted drawing, done without rulers or tracing, and also a licence giving full liberty

explanation.definitionFit: Drawing done without instruments is called this, and the phrase also means unrestricted authority.

clue.text: She interpreted Weill, yet not all 'e composed

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: A singer of Weill's music, though not everything he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian singer-actress, Weill's wife, was the foremost performer of his songs.

clue.text: Philip II's complex putting off callers? That is nothing!

indicators.note: putting off suggests the letters are disturbed and set in a different order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Spanish king's psychological hang-up is deterring visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' reads as a psychological hang-up, but it is a building complex.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal monastery-palace near Madrid was built by Philip II of Spain.

clue.text: One makes things compatible, fitting between a daughter and the common woman

indicators.note: the word for fitting sits between the earlier pieces and the last one

parts.note: 'er is a common, dropped-aitch pronunciation of her
fitting means apt

explanation.surface: A plug converter fitted between a girl and her mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that lets otherwise mismatched plugs or parts connect is called this.

clue.text: Concerning Kate's float?

parts.note: re means concerning
Kate Adie is a well-known BBC war reporter

explanation.surface: Asks about a reporter's parade vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A float is the ready cash kept in a till for change, not a parade vehicle or a raft.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money, cash in hand, is slang for the change kept in a till.

clue.text: Works of Blue Period with aural insert

indicators.note: the word for aural is an insert, put into the word for period

parts.note: an era is a period
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: Picasso's Blue Period canvases with a sound track added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue Period' suggests Picasso, but 'Blue' means smutty and 'Period' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica are works of sexual content, which blue in British usage describes.

clue.text: My crime sat unsettled and out of order

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: My crime sat uneasily and broke the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lopsided, with parts not matching, lacks orderly balance.

clue.text: Wonder at disparity in trade with East

parts.note: a trade gap is the difference between imports and exports

explanation.surface: Marvelling at the trade imbalance with the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare open-mouthed is to show wonder, an amazed look.

clue.text: Hard on a pieceworker's liver

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a bit is a piece
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A tough job is wearing on a piece-rate worker's internal organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liver' looks like the organ but means one who lives somewhere, a resident.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lives in a place is an inhabitant or resident.

clue.text: Charge card not for a gringo?

parts.note: a gringo is an American, abbreviated Am
ex means without, so not for or not belonging to

explanation.surface: A credit card that a foreigner cannot use.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of the American Express card reads as Am-ex, a former American.
explanation.definitionFit: American Express issues a well-known charge card, known by this short name.

clue.text: One of Putin's 16

parts.note: 16 is the across clue meaning cash, so this is one unit of the Russian leader's money

explanation.definitionFit: This is the basic currency unit of Russia, which Putin led.

clue.text: Sally! One's not out to get it!

definitions.text: Sally! One's not out to get it!

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is not out is in
a sally is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: A quip that only insiders can understand.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a joke only those 'in' the group understand; IN, a batter not dismissed in cricket, plus JOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip understood only by members of a particular circle.

clue.text: Mustard to singe one's hair?

parts.note: to char is to singe or scorch
a lock is a tress of hair, a piece of one's hair

explanation.surface: Burning a strand of your hair with mustard.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered weed is wild mustard, a plant of the cabbage family.
